extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A texture dataset created using text-to-image models, spanning 246,285 texture images across 56 texture classes. The dataset is generated from constructed descriptive prompts and refined through frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring to improve quality and representativeness.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak and Patrick McDaniel
extraction.citeAs: Hoak, Blaine, and Patrick McDaniel. On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created in three steps. First, the authors constructed texture-specific prompts by combining descriptors across texture classes. Second, these prompts were used as input to Stable Diffusion model pipelines to generate images, regenerating images flagged by the NSFW filter until 5 non-flagged images per prompt were obtained. Third, the generated images were refined using frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP score filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of synthetic images generated from 96,768 unique text prompts using Stable Diffusion. The prompts were built from 56 texture classes and descriptor categories including artistic, spatial, enhancer, and color words.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged by the Stable Diffusion NSFW safety filter were regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images. Flagged images were temporarily recorded by disabling the filter for analysis, but were excluded from the final dataset and not released publicly. The generated images were then filtered in three stages: retaining the top 80% by frequency cutoff within each texture class, filtering out the bottom 20% by mean patch variance within each texture class, and filtering out the bottom 20% by CLIP score within each texture class.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were structured by combining one word from each descriptor category in standard English adjective order. Generated images were refined by computing Fourier transforms and retaining images with higher high-frequency content, dividing images into non-overlapping 50x50 patches and removing images with low variance across patch means, and using CLIP cosine similarity between image and prompt embeddings to remove poorly aligned images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A human evaluation was conducted with 9 participants. Each participant was shown 100 images in random order and asked two questions for each image: how they would rate the overall quality of the image and how well the image represented the provided descriptor. Ratings were given on a scale of 1 to 5. A total of 900 unique images were evaluated, selected before refinement so scores could be compared across refinement stages. Participants could also optionally comment on trends they observed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors computed mean human quality and representativeness scores across images at different stages of the refinement process. They compared scores before and after each refinement stage and found gradual improvement at each step, with an overall 3.4% increase in quality and 4.5% increase in representativeness. They also analyzed prompt trends using representative scores, participant comments, and CLIP scores, and noted alignment between human representative scores and CLIP scores.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses that the dataset supports research on interpretability, bias analysis, robustness, and model trustworthiness. It highlights use in measuring texture bias and enabling new metrics such as Texture Object Association Values (TAV), which can uncover associations between textures and objects and study their impact on model predictions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses texture bias in models rather than demographic bias in the dataset. It also notes that Stable Diffusion's NSFW safety filter was highly sensitive to texture data, with up to 60% of initial generated images being flagged despite benign prompts, indicating a broader filtering issue with abstract or texture-based content. Fourier analysis suggested the final dataset was not overly biased toward a certain frequency.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Stable Diffusion is not explicitly designed to create textures, so object-like images may arise during generation. The paper notes variation in quality across texture classes, with more structured textures such as grid and polka-dotted tending to have worse scores, indicating room for improvement in generating structured textures. The authors also excluded all images flagged by the NSFW filter from the final dataset and public release for ethical reasons, even though they found no explicit content in them.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for texture-based research and applications, including understanding high-level features learned by models, uncovering biases, identifying security vulnerabilities, constructing texture-object associations, and measuring texture bias. It is also described as a resource for advancing interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning.
